short: The interwoven civilisations of Greece and Rome around the Mediterranean.
full:
Classical Antiquity spans roughly 800 BCE to 500 CE, running in parallel with the later Iron Age rather than after it. It opens with the Greek city-states and the Homeric epics, and takes in Athenian democracy, Greek philosophy, mathematics and drama, and the conquests of Alexander.

Rome then absorbed and transmitted that inheritance across an empire encircling the Mediterranean, adding engineering, codified law and a common administrative language. The period conventionally ends around 500 CE with the fall of the Western Roman Empire, though the Eastern Empire continued for another thousand years from Constantinople.
